rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived fresh, not inherited from the prior run's stale line numbers (54/60/137, now shifted to 56/62/139 after the Pocock-paragraph-added / Willison-sentence-cut edit). Chunk 5 line 56: "Two artefacts in the Amp surface, with different bylines and different shapes." and line 62: "What's distinctive about the Amp surface: composition seams ship inside Amp's runtime..." Chunk 9 line 139: "If your team has standardised on Amp's runtime, Metcalf and the Amp surface by default." Harm check: §8 bans 'surface as noun ("writing surface")' as maintainer dialect, distinct from cleared verb usage. 'The Amp surface' is noun usage and is NOT the same shape as an established engineering compound like 'API surface' or 'attack surface' — those pair 'surface' with a technical boundary noun; 'Amp surface' pairs it with a company name to mean 'the things Amp ships/publishes,' which is exactly this repo's own coinage pattern ('writing surface', 'buyer-facing surface') applied to a new referent. By contrast, line 77 'the human's existing tool surface' is left unflagged: 'tool surface' tracks the established attack-surface-style idiom (the footprint of available tools) and an engineer parses it without repo context. The harm — dialect a room projects and cannot parse cleanly — is present for 'the Amp surface' specifically.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Swap 'the Amp surface' for 'Amp' or 'the Amp surface area of publications' only where the plainer noun loses no meaning — likely just 'Amp' reads clean in all three spots.

rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Chunk 1: unbold the sentences, keep only the practitioner/framework name as a short handle if anything. Chunk 8: keep bold on the 1-2 handles the slide most needs (e.g. 'A single orchestrator') and flatten the rest to plain prose leads.
